section: International climate initiatives - UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, CDM, Paris Agreement, key COP outcomes, IPCC assessment reports
subsections: CDM in India and negotiating blocs
Climate initiatives launched at COPs - founders

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and carbon credits?
o: CDM dealt with ozone-depleting substances and generated HFC credits
CDM projects in developing countries earned Certified Emission Reductions (CERs)
CDM applied exclusively to developed countries and generated Assigned Amount Units
CDM projects earned only renewable-energy certificates issued under the Paris Agreement
accepted.x: CDM projects in developing countries such as India earned Certified Emission Reductions, or CERs. The CDM is now being replaced by the Article 6.4 Paris Agreement Crediting Mechanism (PACM).
accepted.tq: Use the exact mechanism-unit association and distinguish Kyoto mechanisms from Paris mechanisms.
accepted.sec: CDM in India and negotiating blocs

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Bloc — Members or position
1. BASIC — Brazil, South Africa, India and China
2. LMDC — Like-Minded Developing Countries, including India
3. AOSIS — Small island states pressing for the 1.5°C goal
4. G77 and China — The main developing-country group

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. BASIC consists of Brazil, South Africa, India and China; India is also a member of LMDC, while AOSIS represents small island states and G77 plus China is the principal developing-country group.
accepted.tq: Check each bloc against its membership or negotiating position before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: CDM in India and negotiating blocs

accepted.s: At SB64 held in Bonn from 8 to 18 June 2026, India aligned itself with which of the following groups?
o: BASIC, LMDC and G77 plus China
G7, V20 and the European Union
AOSIS, G7 and V20
BASIC, AOSIS and the Least Developed Countries group
accepted.x: At SB64 in Bonn, India aligned with G77 plus China, LMDC and BASIC. It also sought a dedicated agenda slot for the provision requiring developed countries to provide finance.
accepted.tq: Recall the country-to-bloc association and avoid substituting unrelated climate coalitions.
accepted.sec: CDM in India and negotiating blocs

accepted.s: India sought dedicated agenda space at SB64 for discussion of which Paris Agreement provision?
o: Article 9.1 on finance by developed countries
Article 28 on withdrawal from the Agreement
Article 13 on Biennial Transparency Reports
Article 6.4 on the PACM
accepted.x: India requested dedicated agenda space for Article 9.1, which obliges developed countries to provide climate finance to developing countries. Article 13 concerns transparency, while Article 28 concerns withdrawal.
accepted.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish provisions dealing with finance, transparency and withdrawal.
accepted.sec: CDM in India and negotiating blocs

accepted.s: Which one of the following treaties addresses greenhouse gases directly through emission-reduction commitments?
o: Stockholm Convention
Kyoto Protocol
Rotterdam Convention
Basel Convention
accepted.x: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, addresses greenhouse-gas reductions. The Basel, Stockholm and Rotterdam Conventions deal respectively with hazardous waste, persistent organic pollutants and hazardous chemicals or pesticides.
accepted.tq: Use treaty-subject matching to eliminate conventions dealing with waste, pollutants or chemicals.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Montreal Protocol primarily addresses ozone-depleting substances, although some such substances are also greenhouse gases.
2. The Paris Agreement addresses global warming through nationally determined contributions.
3. The Minamata Convention addresses mercury.
4. The Stockholm Convention addresses persistent organic pollutants.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Montreal Protocol has an indirect greenhouse-gas relevance because CFCs are greenhouse gases, while the other statements correctly identify the subjects of the Paris, Minamata and Stockholm instruments.
accepted.tq: Separate the principal subject of each treaty from its indirect environmental relevance.

accepted.s: Which one of the following treaties is correctly matched with its principal subject?
o: Basel Convention — hazardous waste movement
Rotterdam Convention — mercury pollution
Minamata Convention — prior informed consent for pesticides
Stockholm Convention — ozone-depleting substances
accepted.x: The Basel Convention concerns the movement of hazardous waste. The Rotterdam Convention concerns prior informed consent for hazardous chemicals and pesticides, the Minamata Convention concerns mercury, and the Stockholm Convention concerns persistent organic pollutants.
accepted.tq: Spot the swapped treaty subject, a common wrong-authority or wrong-body trap.

accepted.s: One carbon credit generally represents:
o: One tonne of methane emitted into the atmosphere
One tonne of carbon dioxide released under an emission cap
One tonne of coal replaced by renewable energy
One tonne of carbon dioxide-equivalent reduced, avoided or removed
accepted.x: One carbon credit represents one tonne of carbon dioxide-equivalent emissions reduced, avoided or removed. CDM units are called Certified Emission Reductions (CERs).
accepted.tq: Read the unit precisely and distinguish a reduction or removal from an emission.

accepted.s: India signed the Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan in August 2025 under which provision of the Paris Agreement?
o: Article 6.2
Article 9.1
Article 6.4
Article 14
accepted.x: India signed the Joint Crediting Mechanism with Japan in August 2025 under Article 6.2. India also adopted its Rules of Implementation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the cooperative approaches of Article 6.2 and the central mechanism of Article 6.4.

accepted.s: The next new nationally determined contributions under the five-year Paris cycle, referred to as ‘NDC 3.0’, were due for:
o: COP28 in 2023
COP27 in 2022
COP30 in 2025
COP26 in 2021
accepted.x: New NDCs are submitted every five years. The NDC 3.0 cycle was due for COP30 in 2025.
accepted.tq: Match the numbered NDC cycle with the specified COP year.

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with Article 13 of the Paris Agreement?
o: The Enhanced Transparency Framework and Biennial Transparency Reports
The Global Stocktake every five years
The obligation to provide finance under Article 9.1
Withdrawal from the Agreement after notice
accepted.x: Article 13 establishes the Enhanced Transparency Framework, including common reporting through Biennial Transparency Reports. The first reports were due by the end of 2024.
accepted.tq: Use article-number discrimination to separate transparency, stocktake, finance and withdrawal provisions.

accepted.s: Under Article 28 of the Paris Agreement, a party may withdraw from the Agreement:
o: Three years after entry into force, with withdrawal taking effect one year after notice
Immediately after ratification, with effect on the same day
Only after unanimous consent of all other parties
Five years after entry into force, with effect after six months
accepted.x: A party may give notice of withdrawal three years after the Agreement entered into force for it, and the withdrawal takes effect one year after the notice. Unanimous consent is not required.
accepted.tq: Track the two separate time periods instead of merging the eligibility period with the effective period.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the United States’ withdrawal and re-entry timeline under the Paris Agreement?
o: Withdrawal announced in 2017, effective on 4 November 2020, and re-entry on 19 February 2021
Withdrawal announced in 2016, effective on 1 January 2017, and re-entry in 2020
Withdrawal announced in 2018, effective on 4 November 2019, and re-entry in 2022
Withdrawal announced in 2017, effective on 19 February 2021, and re-entry on 4 November 2020
accepted.x: The United States announced withdrawal in 2017, its withdrawal became effective on 4 November 2020, and it rejoined on 19 February 2021. The dates in the other options are interchanged or incorrect.
accepted.tq: Use first, effective and re-entry dates in sequence; beware of reversed dates.

accepted.s: Which of the following was a historic outcome of COP27 held at Sharm el-Sheikh?
o: Adoption of the UAE Consensus calling for transition away from fossil fuels
Establishment of loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund
Creation of the Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan
Conclusion of the first Global Stocktake
accepted.x: COP27 produced a historic decision to establish loss and damage funding arrangements, including a fund. The UAE Consensus and the first Global Stocktake were outcomes of COP28.
accepted.tq: Distinguish COP27 outcomes from the later COP28 outcomes.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mitigation Work Programme associated with COP27:
1. It extends from COP27 to 2030.
2. It provides for at least two global dialogues every year.
3. Parties were urged to strengthen their 2030 targets by the end of 2023.
4. It called for phasing down unabated coal and phasing out inefficient fossil-fuel subsidies.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe elements of the Mitigation Work Programme. It runs to 2030, includes at least two global dialogues annually and urges stronger 2030 action.
accepted.tq: Test the programme through its duration, frequency, deadline and policy measures.

accepted.s: COP27 reaffirmed the objective of keeping the increase in global average temperature:
o: Below 1.5°C as a legally binding immediate limit
Well below 2°C while pursuing efforts towards 1.5°C
Exactly at 1°C by 2030
Below 3°C without any reference to 1.5°C
accepted.x: COP27 reaffirmed the goal of keeping warming well below 2°C and pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C. It did not replace these targets with an exact 1°C limit.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between ‘well below 2°C’ and the pursuit of the 1.5°C goal.

accepted.s: Which one of the following was associated with the Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda?
o: Thirty-five outcomes for one billion people by 2025
A methane reduction target of 30 per cent from 2020 levels
Thirty outcomes for four billion people by 2030
A target of 11,000 GW renewable capacity by 2030
accepted.x: The Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda contained 30 outcomes intended to benefit 4 billion people by 2030. The renewable-capacity and methane targets belong to other initiatives.
accepted.tq: Match the initiative with its distinctive figures and avoid importing targets from other climate initiatives.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: AWARe — water initiative associated with COP27
MARS — global renewable-capacity pledge of COP28
Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda — methane satellite alert system
Mitigation Work Programme — clean-cooking credit project in Myanmar
accepted.x: AWARe was a water initiative associated with COP27. MARS was UNEP’s methane satellite alert system, while the other pairings combine unrelated initiatives.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure initiative-purpose pair and reject cross-linked distractors.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:

Initiative — Founders or leadership
1. International Drought Resilience Alliance — Spain and Senegal
2. Global Methane Pledge — United States and European Union
3. Glasgow Breakthroughs — United Kingdom-led with world leaders
4. Global Shield against Climate Risks — G7 and V20

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. The first two initiatives listed were launched at COP27 and the latter two at COP26, with the Glasgow Breakthroughs led by the United Kingdom with world leaders.
accepted.tq: Match each initiative with its founders before considering the COP at which it was launched.
accepted.sec: Climate initiatives launched at COPs - founders

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Global Methane Pledge is correct?
o: It was launched at COP28 by India and Japan and seeks a 30 per cent cut from 2015 levels by 2030.
It was launched at COP26 by the United States and the European Union and seeks a 30 per cent cut from 2020 levels by 2030.
It was launched at COP27 by G7 and V20 and targets methane neutrality by 2040.
It was launched at COP26 by Spain and Senegal and addresses drought resilience.
accepted.x: The Global Methane Pledge was launched at COP26 by the United States and the European Union and aims to cut methane emissions by 30 per cent from 2020 levels by 2030. India is not a member.
accepted.tq: Check the launch COP, founders, baseline year and target together; one swapped detail makes an option wrong.
accepted.sec: Climate initiatives launched at COPs - founders

accepted.s: The sector goals of the Glasgow Breakthroughs include all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Power
Steel and hydrogen
Mercury management
Road transport
accepted.x: The Glasgow Breakthroughs cover power, road transport, steel, hydrogen and agriculture. Mercury management is associated with the Minamata Convention, not the Glasgow Breakthroughs.
accepted.tq: Find the item that belongs to a different environmental treaty or subject.
accepted.sec: Climate initiatives launched at COPs - founders

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the UAE Consensus adopted at COP28?
o: It replaced nationally determined contributions with legally fixed national quotas.
It was the first decision to establish the Kyoto Protocol’s CDM.
It limited the Global Stocktake to once every ten years.
It was the first COP decision calling for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems.
accepted.x: The UAE Consensus was the first COP decision calling for a transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems. It also followed the conclusion of the first Global Stocktake at COP28.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive wording of the COP28 decision and reject substitutions from Kyoto or Paris procedures.

accepted.s: Which of the following energy pledges was associated with COP28?
o: Reducing renewable capacity to 4,000 GW and increasing efficiency gains to 11 per cent annually
Cutting methane by 30 per cent from 2020 levels and phasing out all coal by 2025
Providing 30 adaptation outcomes for four billion people by 2030
Tripling renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and doubling energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent annually by 2030
accepted.x: COP28 included pledges to triple renewable capacity to 11,000 GW and double energy-efficiency gains to 4 per cent per year by 2030. The other options combine targets from different initiatives or alter the figures.
accepted.tq: Pair the two numerical targets and their deadline; beware of reversed or borrowed figures.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about COP28 is correct?
o: It operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund and concluded the first Global Stocktake.
It first established the COP27 Mitigation Work Programme and the Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda.
It launched the Global Methane Pledge with India as a member.
It created the Article 28 withdrawal procedure of the Paris Agreement.
accepted.x: COP28 concluded the first Global Stocktake and operationalised the Loss and Damage Fund. The Mitigation Work Programme and Sharm el-Sheikh Adaptation Agenda are associated with COP27, while Article 28 is a provision of the Paris Agreement.
accepted.tq: Use the COP-number timeline to separate outcomes belonging to COP27, COP28 and the Paris Agreement itself.
